# MODULE 2: KNOW YOUR CUSTOMER (KYC)  
## What Is KYC?  
**KYC = Know Your Customer**  
KYC rules require banks to:
1. Collect customer identity information
2. Verify customer identity
3. Understand customer's business/source of funds
4. Assess customer's risk level

raw_entities.description: A training module covering the Know Your Customer (KYC) regulatory framework and its core requirements. The module defines the four foundational KYC obligations: collection of customer identity information, verification of customer identity, understanding of customer business and source of funds, and assessment of customer risk level.
context: KYC rules require banks to: 1. Collect customer identity information 2. Verify customer identity 3. Understand customer's business/source of funds 4. Assess customer's risk level

raw_entities.name: Collect Customer Identity Information
raw_entities.description: Staff must understand and be able to execute the requirement to collect customer identity information as part of the KYC process.

raw_entities.name: Verify Customer Identity
raw_entities.description: Staff must be able to verify customer identity through appropriate documentation and processes as mandated by KYC rules.

raw_entities.name: Understand Customer Business and Source of Funds
raw_entities.description: Staff must understand and assess the customer's business activities and the legitimate source of their funds as part of KYC due diligence.

raw_entities.name: Assess Customer Risk Level
raw_entities.description: Staff must be able to evaluate and classify the risk level of a customer based on collected KYC information.
